sentence_of_record: GRANULARITY-GT (2026-10-04, 0 calls) — VALID; GR1 MIXED, GR2 HELD, F-GR not fired. On the [LF] intent trees (MASSIVE 4,946 EVAL items, 84 leaves; CLINC 6,672, 139 leaves), the tree's dendrogram purity against the coarse gold level lies above the 97.5th percentile of 200 matched-shape random trees on both corpora (0.670 vs 0.304; 0.477 vs 0.197). At the coarse level the tree's best cut beats average-link on MASSIVE (D1 +0.340 [+0.323, +0.350]) but not on CLINC (NEITHER, D1 -0.023); the MASSIVE comparator is a chained average-link (one leaf holds 85.7% of TRAIN), so this reads 'better than a chained average-link', not 'better than a competent hierarchy'. P1's 'GR1 NEITHER' NOT SCORED.

plain_description.what: On two intent datasets with gold labels (MASSIVE and CLINC), it compares the label-free discovered tree with an average-link clustering hierarchy at the coarse gold level. It also compares the tree's purity with 200 random trees of the same shape. No calls.
plain_description.why: It tests whether the discovered tree reflects real structure ('right at some granularity') rather than arbitrary splits.
plain_description.information: Beating random trees shows real structure. Beating a standard hierarchy would show it is better than an off-the-shelf method. Result: valid. The tree beats random trees of the same shape on both corpora. Against average-link the result is mixed: it wins on MASSIVE, but only against a badly chained comparator, and does not win on CLINC. This shows no routing value and no MMLU-Pro result.
